title: helm(private): stabilize values schema + templating + init-jobs/hooks for upgrade/rollback compatibility
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Stabilizes the Helm chart values schema (v3), adds templating helpers for KMS/tolerations/nodeSelectors, and makes init-hook ordering upgrade-safe. No customer-facing behavioral changes expected; this is mostly chart templates and schema validation improvements.
description: Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in constrained upgrade windows hit flaky init-job ordering and schema validation edge-cases during Helm upgrades. This PR stabilizes the values schema (v3), improves templating for optional KMS/tolerations/nodeSelector configs, and hardens init-hook ordering/rollback behavior so upgrades are safe in the presence of partial resource creation. Changes: 1) Add values.schema.json (v3) with explicit kubeResource/email/backups sections and deprecation warnings for legacy fields. 2) Introduce templating helpers (_helpers.tpl) for optional tolerations/nodeSelector/KMS to reduce conditional duplication and ensure deterministic manifests. 3) Convert initjobs (postgres/postgres-backup) to use ordered Helm hooks with failurePolicy: "" and hook-weight to ensure correct sequencing; add pre-upgrade crd-check job to gate rollouts. 4) Add a migration guide in CHARTS.md and a post-upgrade validation job (optional) to detect stale init-job state. 5) Improve tests: chart-verify now runs schema validation, template lint, and a helm upgrade/dry-run matrix covering 3 legacy->v3 upgrade paths. Testing/CI: unit templates run in CI, chart-verify job added to GHA, and an integration job in the perf-canary repo triggered on the chart release candidate. Backwards compatibility: fields marked deprecated map automatically and emit warnings during helm template; rollout paths tested for in-place upgrades and canary rollback scenarios. See linked Linear tickets for context.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Please add a note explaining why we chose hook-weight ordering vs. relying on dependency charts. Priya: hook-weight ensures ordering across resources created within the same chart and is more robust in air-gapped/private installs.

Laura Martinez: CI failed on first run due to schema validator complaining about an extraProperties rule; addressed by tightening the schema and adding migration warnings. Laura: approved after schema fix.

Ethan Zhao: Suggest adding an explicit helm test that detects leftover init-job pods after failed upgrades. Priya: added optional post-upgrade validation job and documented how to enable it for sensitive installs.
Ops (Sebastian): During a dry-run upgrade we saw a templating edge-case with nodeSelector being null; fixed by helper that renders nothing for null/false and a comment in CHARTS.md.

post_merge_notes: Operators: when upgrading from charts < v3 run 'helm template' with --values migration/legacy-mapping.yaml to verify deprecation warnings. If you use custom nodeSelectors/tolerations with templating helpers, set the higher-level 'workloads.defaultTolerations' rather than per-chart injection. Backups: postgres-backup init-job now a hook; ensure existing backup Jobs have completed before applying chart upgrade to avoid duplicate backup runs.

testing_matrix_summary: Validated upgrade paths: legacy-values->v3 (in-place), v2->v3 with migration mapping, fresh install v3. Verified rollback path by simulating failure after post-upgrade hooks and ensuring pre-upgrade hook state allows safe rollback.
